_note: Lab tools. `dataResidency` is required and is rendered before the tool, not buried in a footer. `serverCalls:false` means the page makes no network request with user input — the claim must stay true or the field must change.

items.name: Legacy URL Mapper
items.summary: Paste a list of old URLs. It normalises them, groups query-string patterns, flags duplicates and many-to-one collapses, and proposes a review status for each group. You export CSV and make the decisions yourself.

dataResidency.statement: Everything runs in your browser. Your URLs are never uploaded, logged or stored — there is no request to any server after the page loads, and nothing is written to local storage.

inputs.label: URL list
inputs.note: One URL per line. Absolute or path-only. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.

limits: It groups by path plus the set of parameter names — not by what the page actually returned. Two URLs in the same group may have served different content.
It cannot know which historical parameter values were meaningful. `?script=` matters; `?utm_source=` does not. The tracking-parameter list is editable and incomplete by construction.
Redirect proposals are proposals. `auto` means the group collapsed cleanly to one target, not that the target is correct.
No status codes are fetched. This tool never touches the network.
methodology: Normalise: trim, lowercase the scheme and host, drop the default port, decode percent-escapes once, drop the fragment, sort remaining query parameters by name.
Strip known tracking parameters from the grouping key, but keep them in the record so nothing is silently lost.
Mark a group `duplicate` when two inputs normalise identically, `review` when one group holds more than one distinct value set, and `auto` when the group is unambiguous.
Export every field, including the reason for the status, so the CSV is auditable outside the tool.

items.name: Response Header Inspector
items.summary: Paste a raw response header block and get a readable breakdown of caching, redirect and indexing directives, with the conflicts highlighted.

dataResidency.statement: Planned as local-only. If that ever changes, this page changes first.
